sources.title: Josh Angrist — The Economic Returns to Schooling, MIT 14.661 Fall 2017
sources.use: Brief context for schooling investment and heterogeneous selection; original finite-horizon model and IV population.
sources.verification: Official PDF text inspected, physical pages 1–4, lines 0–142. No figures or empirical estimates adopted.
sources.limits: The heterogeneous optimum condition g_s/g=r is pointwise; we do not adopt a global log-earnings schedule by integrating that condition across different optima.

sources.title: Josh Angrist — Market Structure and the Min, MIT 14.661 Fall 2017

sources.verification: Official PDF text inspected, physical pages 1–3, lines 0–96.
sources.limits: Extracted mathematical minus/infinity glyphs are unreliable. Chapter equations independently derived; no historical estimates, figures or current law claims imported.

sources.title: Marianne Bertrand and Sendhil Mullainathan (2004) — Are Emily and Greg More Employable Than Lakisha and Jamal? A Field Experiment on Labor Market Discrimination
sources.use: Historical randomized-name correspondence design as a bounded methodological reference. All chapter callback counts are synthetic.
sources.verification: Official AEA article identity and abstract read, lines 42–61; AER 94(4), 991–1013.
sources.limits: Full paper, replication files and historical estimates not used or verified. Abstract access establishes the stated design, not all its implementation details.

sources.title: Guido W. Imbens, Joshua D. Angrist — Identification and Estimation of Local Average Treatment Effects (Econometrica62(2), March1994, pages467–475)
sources.use: Binary heterogeneous treatment effects, compliance decomposition and LATE limits. Original finite population and violations are not attributed to the paper.
sources.verification: Reused prior accepted v12-c03 inspection: Rendered PDF pages1–9, printed467–475. Main method scope: Conditions1–3, signed response decomposition, Theorem1 and proof, Theorems2–3 and appendix proofs; references inspected as bibliography only. Rendered physical pages 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9. Exact source-byte hash and cautions in reviews/v12-c03-sources.json.
sources.limits: Use a separately stated binary potential-outcome contract with assignment independence, exclusion, consistency, positivity, integrability and positive complier mass. No automatic ATE, treatment-on-treated, multivalued-instrument weighting or transportability claim. The appendix's estimated-instrument covariance warns against ignoring first-stage nuisance estimation. Random assignment of an encouragement does not itself exclude its direct outcome effect. Administrative-selection and historical application examples were read but are neither reproduced nor claimed to establish validity in a new case.

originality: Five original worked cases, ten original exercises with full solutions. Original proofs and counterexamples; sources provide bounded methodological context.
